title: Mysterious Case File — official storefront
authors: Mysterious Case File (operator not named; footer 'Powered by YZ')
publisher: Mysterious Case File (operator not named; footer 'Powered by YZ')
key_findings: Sells physical Arabic boxed murder-mystery case files; prices in Moroccan dirham, cash on delivery in Morocco, card payment for international shipping.
Each case is advertised with 50+ documents (suspect photos, interview transcripts, evidence envelopes, forensic/autopsy reports, witness statements) and three missions; hints on request.
Listed prices (MAD, accessed 2026-10-27): single cases 209 (marked down from 300-320); 'detective box' 464 (from 999); time-limited 30-50% promotion.
Self-describes as the first investigation game in the Arab world (marketing claim, unverified); no educational claims; no age range published.
athar_applications: Evidence that Arabic-speaking adults/families pay for document-based case files; benchmark for document density (~50 items/case) and multi-mission structure.
ATHAR differentiator vs paper boxes: evidence-linking, reasoning feedback and assessment that paper cannot provide.
limitations: Owner/company not named; no sales volume; age suitability unknown; 'first in Arab world' claim is contested by other sellers making the same claim.

title: Al-Qadiya Al-Ghamida (The Mysterious Case) — Salla store
authors: Unnamed Saudi store (Salla platform; commercial registration shown)
publisher: Unnamed Saudi store (Salla platform; commercial registration shown)
key_findings: Saudi e-store (prices in SAR, cash on delivery inside Saudi Arabia only) selling a 'very realistic' physical case file that casts players as detectives.
Advertises group play for 1-9 players and gatherings with friends; claims shipping to 230+ countries and 24-48h delivery.
Homepage publishes no price, case count, age range or detailed mechanics; makes no educational claims.
athar_applications: Confirms a Saudi market for social/group Arabic case-file play — relevant to ATHAR co-op and 'majlis' group modes.
limitations: Thin public information; owner not named; mechanics and catalog size unknown.

title: Malaf Serry (Secret File) — Unsolved Case Files Game store
key_findings: Egyptian-dialect store priced in EGP: single cases LE 450 each; two-case bundle LE 599 (marked down from LE 900) as accessed 2026-10-27.
Case files contain witness and suspect statements with photos, full crime details and scene evidence; player identifies the culprit.
Claims the game builds observation and reasoning skills, with no supporting evidence; offers a free-play section and a how-to-play blog; sells via Facebook/Instagram/TikTok.
athar_applications: Price anchor for Egypt; dialect copywriting as a localization choice; social-commerce distribution (TikTok/Instagram) used by small Arab sellers.
limitations: Owner unnamed; physical vs digital format not stated; catalog size unclear; skill claims unsubstantiated.

title: Sara's Case — digital file (PDF), FILE ZERO
key_findings: Digital-only 12-page PDF case sold for 19 SAR: suspect profiles, investigation records, forensic reports, a police report and victim diary excerpts; rated easy with 2 suspects.
Answer checking is done by scanning a barcode at the end of the file that reveals the solution.
Store branding is inconsistent: listing names the seller 'FILE ZERO' while the store title/slug is 'Firasa'.
athar_applications: Lowest observed price anchor for a single Arabic digital case (19 SAR).
Barcode answer-reveal is the primitive version of the verification step ATHAR must upgrade to reasoning-quality feedback.
limitations: Country inferred from SAR pricing; catalog size and sales unknown; no age guidance.

title: Circle of Suspicion — official website
authors: Mahmoud Al-Nimr / Al-Nimr Digital Solutions (النمر للحلول الرقمية)
publisher: Mahmoud Al-Nimr / Al-Nimr Digital Solutions (النمر للحلول الرقمية)
key_findings: Arabic-first detective game playable in the browser and via an Android app with one shared account; English toggle available.

Mechanics: explore scenes, collect evidence, take notes, interrogate suspects, then submit the culprit together with supporting evidence; daily challenge, competitive multiplayer, collectible cards, themes.
An AI assistant, stated to run on Google Gemini, analyses evidence with the player and gives hints without revealing the solution; the site does not claim AI generates cases.
Case-count claims are inconsistent on the same site (14 listed; 24; 185; '+50'); free registration and some free cases; no educational claims (entertainment: mystery, crime, horror).
athar_applications: Closest Arabic analogue to ATHAR's core loop; shows an AI hint layer on a general LLM is already cheap and copyable.
'Accuse with supporting evidence' is a mechanic ATHAR should match and then exceed with argument-quality scoring.
limitations: Self-published claims; no ratings or usage data on site; inconsistent case counts lower trust; no age rating stated on site.

title: دائرة الشك (Circle of Suspicion) — Google Play listing
key_findings: Developer listed as NEMER DIGITAL SOLUTIONS, Cairo, Egypt; description claims 245+ cases (murder, heists, disappearances, cybercrime, historical investigations).
1K+ downloads, no visible star rating, last updated 1 Aug 2026, content rating Everyone, ad-free, in-app purchases (prices not shown) — as accessed 2026-10-27.
Data-safety declaration: no data collected or shared; encrypted in transit; deletion on request (developer self-declaration).
athar_applications: Shows the closest Arabic competitor is still very small (1K+ installs) — the Arabic digital detective niche is not yet captured.
limitations: Store data are snapshots; 'Everyone' rating sits awkwardly with horror positioning on the website; data-safety claims are self-declared and unverified.

title: ملف القضية: حقق في 1000 جريمة — Google Play listing
key_findings: Arabic text-based detective app with 'hundreds' of cases (theft, sabotage, disappearances, puzzles).

Mechanics: read case summaries, compare suspects' accounts before/during/after the incident, tap key words in the text to reveal hidden clues, arrange evidence in an investigation box, accuse within limited attempts.
Scores players with an 'IQ-style' accuracy score and leaderboard; claims to reward observation and deduction over speed.
100+ downloads; updated 24 Aug 2026; rated 7+; contains ads (accessed 2026-10-27).
athar_applications: 'Tap a word to surface a clue' and timeline comparison are cheap, text-native mechanics suited to Arabic mobile reading.
Cautionary example: IQ framing is a scientifically weak claim ATHAR should avoid in favour of skill-specific feedback.
limitations: Tiny install base; rating not shown; case quality and fairness unknown.

title: Detective CrimeBot: Mysteries — Google Play listing (Arabic store page)
topics: global detective app in Arabic stores
key_findings: Italian-developed detective game with 1M+ installs and 4.3 stars (header shows 17.3K reviews; review section 15.9K) on Google Play, accessed 2026-10-27; last updated 26 Nov 2025; rated Everyone 10+; ads and in-app purchases.
The Arabic-language store page describes a crime-scene system combining hidden objects, clues, suspects, witnesses, motives and relationships in 'endless combinations' (i.e., generated cases).
Players investigate, then accuse; wrong accusations cost points (per reviews summarised on the page).
athar_applications: Proof that a generated-case detective game already reaches Arabic-store users at scale; direct benchmark for ATHAR's generated-vs-handcrafted decision.
Weakness to exploit: Western sci-fi setting, no learning claims, no reasoning assessment.
limitations: Google Play page does not list in-game languages (Arabic support confirmed on App Store listing ATH-SRC-1108); review counts inconsistent on page; no data on Arab-country share of installs.

title: المحقق - التحقيق الجنائي (Detective CrimeBot) — App Store listing
key_findings: App Store lists Arabic plus 19 other languages; Arabic app title; age 13+; 4.2 stars from 153 ratings (US store); free with in-app purchases; version 2.0.8 dated 30 Jul 2024.

Premise: detective for the 'CrimeBot' agency in 2049 Scotland; a system creates crime scenes with hidden objects, clues, suspects, witnesses, motives and relationships in endless combinations; changelog notes improved clue generation by difficulty level; limited attempts before the killer escapes.
athar_applications: Confirms full Arabic localization of a generated-case detective game — ATHAR cannot claim 'first Arabic detective app with generated cases'.
limitations: Ratings are US-store; Arab-store ratings not captured; App Store and Play update dates differ.

title: Tamatem Games — official site and 'Our Games' page
key_findings: Amman-based publisher bringing international mobile games to the Arabic-speaking market; genres listed include cards, strategy, MMORPG, story-narratives and trivia.
The 'Our Games' page (accessed 2026-10-27) lists 9 titles (e.g., Awad Delivery King 2, VIP Baloot, Fashion Queen, Hoson); none is mystery, detective, interactive fiction or educational.
athar_applications: Candidate publishing/localization/UA partner for a consumer ATHAR app.
White-space signal: the leading Arabic mobile publisher's current list has no detective/mystery title.
limitations: Games page may not be the full historic catalog (older titles such as 'Mystery of the Past' appear only in third-party summaries); no player numbers on site.

title: Jordanian entrepreneur built Tamatem into a regional key player in the gaming industry (Forbes Middle East, reposted)
authors: Tamatem (repost of Forbes Middle East article by Samuel Wendel)
publisher: Tamatem (repost of Forbes Middle East article by Samuel Wendel)
key_findings: Model: partner with foreign developers, localize and publish for MENA on revenue share; localization can take ~2 weeks to under 2 months; shifted toward publishing in late 2016 as faster/cheaper than in-house.
Self-reported 2017 figures: ~50 games released, 40M+ downloads, ~500K daily users.
Founder and an Endeavor Jordan representative argue global studios made few if any games designed for Arab audiences; localized cultural cues performed well.
athar_applications: Supports the cultural-relevance thesis for Arabic-original content; indicates localization partners can move fast.
limitations: 2017 data; self-reported; reposted on company site; publisher has since changed (later funding/ownership not verified here).

title: 25 Arab games showcased at Arabic Games Conference 2025
topics: game studios KSA Jordan Iraq Qatar
key_findings: Lists 25 Arab-made games showcased at the Arabic Games Conference 2025 (article dated 29 Nov 2025), many from Saudi studios, plus Jordan, Iraq and Qatar.

Some mystery/puzzle titles (My Father Lied — Lunar Games, Iraq; The Circle Move — OONY Team, Saudi Arabia; Operation Stutter — Kevir Entertainment, Iraq), but none is described as educational or as a detective-reasoning game.
athar_applications: Pool of regional studios/artists for co-production; white-space signal for educational mystery in the Arab indie scene.
limitations: Secondary report; event dates and organizer not stated in article; showcase is a curated subset, not the whole market.

title: Arab Indie Games — curated list
key_findings: Curated directory claiming 292 Arab indie games released 2014-2026.

On the first visible page (13 titles) none is tagged detective, mystery, investigation or educational; nearest: MathPunk Chronicles (Kiddo Interactive, Morocco — math-puzzle narrative) and Owl Logic Puzzle Game (Digital Dunes, Qatar — deduction logic puzzler).
athar_applications: Directory for partner/talent scouting; supports 'no dominant Arab educational mystery title' hypothesis.
limitations: Only the first page inspected; editorial picks, not exhaustive; absence of tags is not proof of absence.

title: Top Visual Novel games available in Arabic — itch.io
key_findings: itch.io returned 24 visual novels flagged as available in Arabic (accessed 2026-10-27).

Detective titles in the list are mostly non-Arab (Crimebot 2 by RoboBot Studio; Tangle Tower by SFBGames); one Arab-made investigative title: 'The Official Story' (A.M. Games) — an Egyptian journalist uncovering corruption.
athar_applications: Arabic interactive fiction supply on open indie platforms is very thin — a content gap ATHAR can fill.
limitations: Language flags are self-declared by developers; snapshot only; itch.io is a niche channel.

title: Return of the Obra Dinn — Steam store page
key_findings: Released 18 Oct 2018; Steam lists 14 languages including Arabic (interface and subtitles; full audio English only).
athar_applications: A top-tier deduction game is playable in Arabic — sets the quality bar Arab players can already access.
limitations: Steam language table is developer-declared; quality of Arabic translation and RTL rendering not assessed.

title: Disco Elysium — The Final Cut — Steam store page
key_findings: Released 15 Oct 2019; Steam lists 13 languages including Arabic (interface and subtitles; no Arabic voice).
athar_applications: Narrative-heavy detective RPG available in Arabic text — evidence that premium global studios do localize into Arabic.
limitations: Mature content (not teen-appropriate); translation quality not assessed.

title: The Case of the Golden Idol — Steam store page
key_findings: Released 13 Oct 2022; 12 supported languages listed (incl. Turkish, Japanese, Korean, Polish); Arabic is not listed.
athar_applications: One of the most-cited modern deduction designs is not available in Arabic — localization gap for fill-in-the-blank deduction.
limitations: Snapshot of Steam page; sequels not checked.

title: Shadows of Doubt — Steam store page
key_findings: Full release 26 Sep 2024 (Early Access from 24 Apr 2023); 9 languages listed; Arabic not supported.
athar_applications: Procedurally generated detective sandbox not available in Arabic.
limitations: Snapshot of Steam page.

title: Criminal Case: Hidden Objects — App Store listing
key_findings: App Store lists English plus 11 languages (incl. Turkish, Indonesian); Arabic not included; rated 16+; 4.7 stars from 36K ratings (US store, accessed 2026-10-27).
Free-to-play with in-app purchases from $0.99 to $9.99 and an optional $2.99/week subscription.
athar_applications: The best-known mobile 'detective' brand is not in Arabic; its F2P/energy model is a monetization reference and a cautionary one for teens.
limitations: US-store data; Arabic-speaking users may still play in English (Arabic blogs review it).

title: MurderMysteryTime — online murder mystery game
key_findings: Browser murder-mystery site whose language menu includes Arabic, but case content observed was in English.
Advertises 24+ handwritten cases, 95 suspects and 124 evidence items; one free full case, Premium subscription for the archive; single accusation, wrong answer reveals solution; no timer.
Targets solo players, couples, friend groups and teachers.
athar_applications: Example of interface-only 'Arabic support' — ATHAR's advantage is native Arabic case writing, not just UI translation.
limitations: Owner and country unknown; Arabic content depth not verified beyond homepage.

title: Launch of the 'Critical Thinking and Philosophy Skills' course for secondary schools (MoE news, 02/04/1440 AH)
title_ar: إطلاق مقرر مهارات التفكير الناقد والفلسفة للمرحلة الثانوية
publisher: Ministry of Education, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
key_findings: In Dec 2018 the Saudi Minister of Education launched a 'Critical Thinking and Philosophy Skills' course for the secondary stage, taught as enrichment from the second semester, initially inside the life-skills curriculum and planned to become standalone.
Tatweer Educational Services and the Ministry trained 200+ teachers and 34 supervisors to deliver it in 200 secondary schools; content prepared with local specialists and a foreign strategic team.
Programme built on four pillars: emotional, cooperative, creative and critical thinking; linked to the character-building programme and Vision 2030.
athar_applications: Strongest verified policy hook in the Gulf for selling ATHAR cases as critical-thinking practice material to schools.
Alignment target: map ATHAR reasoning skills to the course pillars for B2B pitches.
limitations: 2018 announcement; current (2026) status, grade placement and syllabus not verified this session; a 2022 Asharq Al-Awsat back-to-school report did not mention it (absence is not proof of discontinuation).

title: Alef Education expands Alef Pathways to accelerate student progress across subjects and languages (press release)
key_findings: 18 Aug 2026: Alef Pathways (self-paced adaptive supplemental programme) expands to Science, Arabic Reading and English Reading for 2026-27, after Math use in 200 UAE public schools.
Self-reported scale: ~20,000 schools in UAE and Indonesia, ~2.0M registered students, 85,000+ educators.
No mention of critical thinking, inquiry or simulations.
athar_applications: Alef owns the UAE public-school channel for adaptive core-subject practice — a potential distribution partner, and a competitor if it adds case-based science inquiry.
limitations: Press release (self-reported); scale figures differ slightly from another Alef release (ATH-SRC-1122).

title: Alef Education scales AI learning reach across UAE private schools, boosting Arabic proficiency (press release)
key_findings: Arabits (AI-powered Arabic learning) reaches 124,500 students across UAE private school groups; product family: Alef Platform, Alef Pathways, Abjadiyat, Arabits.
States company scale as ~2.0M students, 84,000 educators and 19,000 schools across UAE, Indonesia and Morocco.
athar_applications: Shows Alef expanding into private schools and Morocco — overlapping ATHAR's potential B2B channel.
limitations: Undated on page; self-reported; numbers inconsistent with ATH-SRC-1121.

title: Madrasa — free Arabic e-learning platform (official site)
authors: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives
publisher: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives
key_findings: Free Arabic video lessons in science (chemistry, biology, general science) and mathematics for KG-Grade 12, run as an initiative of MBRGI.
Site mentions exercises/applications but no virtual labs, simulations or critical-thinking content.
athar_applications: Free, government-backed science-explainer supply means ATHAR should not compete on explainer video; link to it or partner for background concepts.
limitations: Homepage only; lesson counts not stated.

title: Biggest e-learning platform in the Arab world launched (Gulf News)
key_findings: Madrasa launched in Oct 2018 by Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid; content translated from 5,000 English videos and 11 million words; Arabic, maths and sciences, KG-12, free; target reach 50M students.
athar_applications: Benchmark for scale of free state-funded Arabic science content.
limitations: 2018 report; figures are launch-time targets, not usage.

title: Edraak — school education (K-12) platform
key_findings: Free K-12 platform aligned to Jordanian, Egyptian and Syrian curricula; mathematics first, then English; short videos, lessons, MCQs with hints and short open questions.
Cites a community of 2 million learners; Edraak homepage describes it as an Arabic MOOC platform founded on the initiative of the Queen Rania Foundation.
No critical-thinking, logic, science-experiment or media-literacy content found on the pages checked.
athar_applications: Potential non-profit content/distribution partner in the Levant; confirms gap in reasoning-skills content.
limitations: Only K-12 page and homepage checked; adult catalog may contain soft-skills courses not seen.

title: Jordan's Abwaab acquires Egyptian edtech Eduact (Wamda)
key_findings: 1 Sep 2026: Abwaab (Jordan, founded 2019) — curriculum-aligned online learning and assessments in six MENA markets — acquired Eduact, an Egyptian SaaS for independent teachers/learning centres; second acquisition of 2026 after Apex Education.
No critical-thinking or gamification offering mentioned.
athar_applications: Consolidating exam-prep players control teen attention and parent spend in Egypt/Jordan; potential distribution partner for enrichment content.
limitations: Secondary news; deal value undisclosed; Abwaab site could not be fetched.

title: Noon Academy acquires Almakhfi to strengthen Saudi edtech offering (Wamda)
key_findings: 7 Jul 2026: Noon Academy (Saudi, founded 2013; live classes, AI tools, core subjects, programming, robotics) acquired Almakhfi, a Qudurat/Tahsili exam-prep platform that has supported 250K+ students.
Article cites Noon's SAR 153M (~$40.8M) Series B; timing of that round unclear from the page. No critical-thinking content mentioned.
athar_applications: Qudurat (aptitude) prep is the closest mass-market 'reasoning' spend for Saudi teens — ATHAR could position cases as engaging reasoning practice adjacent to it, but must avoid claiming score gains without evidence.
limitations: Secondary news; user numbers for Noon not stated.

title: Classera — official website
key_findings: Claims 30M+ users and 45+ countries; AI-powered LMS with gamification and personalization pillars; product suite incl. LMS, C-Reality, C-Kids, C-Iqraa, Edumalls.
Testimonials mention Saudi Arabia and Jordan; page lists a San Francisco address.
No critical-thinking, inquiry or virtual-lab features described.
athar_applications: LMS integration/marketplace channel (Edumalls) for distributing ATHAR cases to schools already on Classera.
limitations: Marketing claims; no independent usage data.

title: Little Thinking Minds — official website
key_findings: Products: I Read Arabic (digital reading platform with stories, games, worksheets, assessments), Standard Assessment Program, I Start Arabic (ACTFL-aligned), KG Arabic.
Self-reported 500,000+ students, 800+ schools, 10+ countries, 10M books read.
Claims to stimulate thinking and raise 'thinkers and critics' but publishes no comprehension or reasoning outcome data.
athar_applications: Proven Arabic-content school-sales model; potential partner for reading-comprehension-linked mystery stories for younger teens.
limitations: Self-reported metrics; HQ not stated on page; reasoning claims unsubstantiated.

title: Lamsa — official website
key_findings: Early-childhood learning app (Arabic/English) with games, stories and videos; 14+ years in market per site.
Lamsa Studio: AI tool for teachers to create assignments and game-based assessments aligned to learning outcomes.
No explicit problem-solving or critical-thinking content; no age range or user numbers published.
athar_applications: Not a direct competitor (age mismatch); Lamsa Studio signals Arab EdTechs moving to AI content generation for teachers.
limitations: Homepage only; target ages vague.

title: PraxiLabs — virtual science lab platform (official website, EN and AR)
key_findings: 210+ interactive 3D simulations across biology, chemistry and physics (20+ branches), with an AI lab assistant ('Oxi'), quiz builder, analytics and LMS integration.
Free account offers 3 full simulations; institutions buy full or partial library on custom quotes (no public prices).
Arabic version of the site exists; labs can be customized in other languages on request; 'Forensics' (الطب الشرعي) listed as a topic under the biology lab.
Customer testimonials cited are mainly from universities in Spain, the US and Canada; HQ and founding year not stated on pages checked.
athar_applications: Build-vs-partner input for ATHAR forensic mini-labs: licensing/partnering may be faster than building 3D labs.
Benchmark for institutional pricing model (quote-based) and LMS integration expectations.
limitations: Did not verify Arabic in-sim UI or content of the forensics labs; company origin not confirmed from official pages this session.

title: Misbar — Arabic fact-checking platform (official website)
key_findings: Arabic fact-checking and investigations site using expert journalists and AI tools.
Runs 'Misbar Workshops' to build critical thinking about shared information, with tracks incl. an introduction to news verification linked to schools and a 'how we verify' track for colleges.
Offers a 'سين جيم' true/false quiz section and tools (tweet scanner, browser extension).
athar_applications: Natural partner for ATHAR 'verification cases' (digital-evidence/source-checking mysteries) and for expert review of misinformation content.
limitations: Owner/country not stated on homepage; no reach data; quiz is simple true/false.

title: Fatabyyano — Arabic fact-checking platform (official website)
key_findings: Independent Arabic verification platform launched in 2014; claims to be first in the Middle East.
Has a media-education section, an academy, a guide, a video series and a fellowship; 2020 COVID-19 campaign for Djibouti and Yemen.
athar_applications: Potential content/review partner for misinformation-themed cases.
limitations: Owner/country and IFCN status not stated on page; programme details not visible.

title: Akeed — Jordan Media Credibility Observatory (official website)
key_findings: Project of the Jordan Media Institute, supported by the King Abdullah II Fund for Development; monitors credibility of Jordanian media against published standards.
Publishes a quick news-credibility checklist and pages on verification methodology and principles; no youth games or programmes shown.
athar_applications: Source of Arabic verification vocabulary and checklists to align ATHAR's media-literacy rubric (with permission).
limitations: Homepage only; youth programming not verified.

title: Media and Information Literacy (MIL) Academy — Jordan Media Institute
key_findings: JMI runs an MIL Academy training programme and an MIL caravan; site lists MIL editions for 2023-2025 and a national MIL strategy.

Listed partners include the Ministry of Government Communication, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Higher Education, Ministry of Youth, UNESCO and DW Akademie; JMI states it supported Jordan's first and second national MIL strategies including integrating MIL concepts in education.
athar_applications: Jordan has a formal national MIL strategy — a policy hook and partner network for a verification-mystery module.
limitations: No reach figures; academy target groups not specified; partners are institute-wide, not academy-specific.

title: Bad News — inoculation game page

key_findings: Bad News (DROG, Gusmanson Design and Cambridge) teaches common manipulation techniques by having players act as a fake-news producer.
Listed language versions (14 languages plus regional variants) do not include Arabic; Go Viral! and Harmony Square listed without language details.
athar_applications: Gap: no Arabic version listed for the best-known prebunking game — Arabic-native misinformation cases are white space (verify further before claiming exclusivity).

title: Storytel — UAE site

Prices shown: $9.99/month, $53.64/6 months, $83.88/year (currency symbol $; accessed 2026-10-27). No crime/mystery category surfaced on the landing page.
athar_applications: Audio mystery series are an attention competitor; also a possible channel for ATHAR audio case prologues.
limitations: Landing page only; Arabic catalogue size not stated; Arabic mystery originals not verified.

title: Sowt — MENA podcast network (official website)
key_findings: Independent MENA media/podcast producer with a studio in Amman; 80+ shows, 1,500+ episodes, 44M+ listens, 1M+ downloads/month (self-reported).
Revenue lines: B2B production, sponsorship, voice-over/dubbing, training, studio rental, Sowt+ subscription at $3/month; no show labelled crime/mystery on homepage.
athar_applications: Candidate partner for Arabic voice acting/audio interrogation scenes and audio case trailers.
limitations: Self-reported metrics; homepage only.

title: Thmanyah — official website
key_findings: Saudi media company producing podcasts, documentaries, articles/newsletters and exclusive coverage of Saudi tournaments; newsletters claimed to reach hundreds of thousands daily.
No crime/mystery/investigative content shown on the homepage.
athar_applications: Major youth-attention competitor in KSA and a potential media/marketing partner for ATHAR launches.
limitations: Homepage only; audience figures self-reported.

title: Apple Podcasts — True Crime genre (Saudi Arabia storefront)
key_findings: On 2026-10-27, 4 of 7 'Top Shows' in the Saudi True Crime genre were Arabic-language (سوالف طريق، بودكاست قصص من المحاكم، قضية، ضد مجهول); new Arabic shows include 'صندوق الجرائم - النسخة الصوتية'.

title: قضية (Qadiya) — Mukhtalif Radio podcast, Apple Podcasts
key_findings: Weekly Arabic true-crime show examining social and security phenomena through investigative reporting, with an awareness aim; 67 episodes; active 2025-2026; 4.0 stars from 34 ratings (SA store, 2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Shows regional radio networks producing crime-awareness audio — possible co-production for fictional ATHAR audio cases.

athar_applications: Legal/court storytelling resonates in KSA — supports ATHAR modules on due process, evidence standards and rights.

title: Mawhiba — King Abdulaziz and His Companions Foundation for Giftedness and Creativity (official website)

title: Top escape rooms in Dubai for puzzle pros and clue seekers (MyBayut)
key_findings: Lists 9 Dubai escape-room venues; detective themes include Phobia Dubai 'Sherlock vs Jack the Ripper' (from AED 115 pp) and Escape Hunt Dubai 'Jack the Ripper' (AED 130-200 pp); many venues are horror-themed (e.g., Escape House AED 220 pp).
Age policies not stated for any venue.

title: Escape Hunt — official website
key_findings: Escape Hunt lists escape-room sites in UAE, Qatar and Kuwait (City Hunt also in UAE); Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon not listed.
Promotes corporate team-building; no school/education programme described on the global homepage.
athar_applications: International chain presence in the Gulf = B2B events competitor and possible licensing partner for ATHAR-branded rooms.
limitations: Global homepage only; country pages not fetched (budget exhausted).

title: The Secret Detective — mystery cases (official website)
key_findings: Jordan-based seller of paper ('ورقية') cinematic detective cases for groups of friends: read the case, collect clues, identify the killer; free delivery advertised.
No prices, case count, ages, contact details or educational claims on the homepage.
athar_applications: Confirms the paper case-file format has spread to the Levant (Jordan) as well as KSA, Egypt and Morocco.
limitations: Very thin public information; owner unknown.

title: لغز الجريمة (Crime Puzzle) — App Store listing
key_findings: Arabic-titled murder-deduction puzzle (witnesses, suspects, hidden objects, alibis, weapon; levels and difficulty settings); free; 13+; 4.0 from 11 ratings (DZ store); last version 1.1 on 19 Aug 2021.
Listing metadata shows Japanese as the only language — a metadata inconsistency for an Arabic-titled app.
athar_applications: Example of small Arabic detective apps that launched and stalled — low barrier to entry but weak retention/content pipelines.
limitations: Very small sample; metadata unreliable.

title: Critical thinking and philosophy to be taught in Saudi schools (Arab News)
key_findings: Jan 2019 report: MoE adds critical thinking and philosophy, initially within the 'Life Skills' curriculum and later as an independent course; aims to encourage questioning and respect for differing views; materials described as used in 60+ countries; law and financial literacy planned next.
athar_applications: Secondary confirmation of ATH-SRC-1120 for pitch materials in English.
limitations: 2019 report; grade levels not specified; current status not verified.

title: 3asafeer — Arabic reading platform (official website)
key_findings: Graded Arabic story books narrated by actors, cartoon lessons, games, interactive exercises and worksheets for native and non-native speakers aged 3-18.
Self-reported 2.2M students; lists education-body partners in Jordan, Dubai (KHDA), Morocco and Bahrain; school trial model (1 week teachers, 1 month school); paid family plans, prices not listed.
No explicit comprehension or critical-thinking outcome claims.
athar_applications: Channel/partner for short Arabic mystery readers for 13-15 within school reading programmes.
limitations: Self-reported scale; '#1 platform' is a marketing claim; HQ not stated.

title: Kerning Cultures Network — official website
key_findings: Podcast network producing narrative shows in Arabic and English; partner logos include Louvre, Toyota and UNHCR; Patreon listener support.
No crime/mystery series named on the homepage; HQ and audience size not stated.
athar_applications: Candidate co-producer for high-quality Arabic narrative audio (case trailers, character voice work).
limitations: Homepage only; catalogue and languages per show not verified.

title: 6 top escape rooms in Cairo (CairoScene)
key_findings: 2015 listicle naming six Cairo escape-room operators (Escape Room, Trapped, BreakOut — described as Egypt's first, The Room Egypt, Escapers, Escapology); themes listed are prison, lab, vault, quarantine; no detective themes; some offer corporate team-building and family-friendly modes.
athar_applications: Shows an established escape-room culture in Egypt since at least 2015; physical rooms are generic puzzles, not evidence-reasoning.
limitations: Dated 2015 — venues may have closed or changed; prices and languages not given.

title: Homicide Desk — Steam store page
key_findings: Released 1 Sep 2026; $5.99; English and Arabic with full audio, full right-to-left layout support, plus 8 other languages; Steam: 67% of 94 reviews (seen 2026-10-27).
Hand-written cases; suspects answer free-text questions via an on-device language model 'constrained to the written facts of the case' (no server).

Hands-on forensics (fingerprint alignment, cipher, chromatograph calibration), phone-record and photo analysis, string evidence board, written deductions with penalties for wrong arrest, multiple guilty-party variants.
athar_applications: Closest single competitor found to ATHAR's core loop (truth-bounded AI suspects + forensic mini-labs + written deduction, in Arabic). ATHAR can no longer claim this combination as new; differentiation must move to teen fit, school use and validated reasoning scoring.
limitations: Adult-oriented homicide content with a gambling minigame (in-game currency); 67% positive on a small base; no stated learning claims; PC only.

title: Shu'la Lab — studio website
key_findings: Site meta description: indie game studio from Iraq; makers of Homicide Desk and WarFront.
athar_applications: Places Homicide Desk as an Arab-made competitor and a possible co-production or benchmark partner.
limitations: One-line self-description; size and funding unknown.

title: invsroom (Investigation Room) — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Released 10 Sep 2026; Arabic and English listing; 12+; AI-played suspects who lie, tense up and break when cornered with evidence; deduction board; team rooms by invite code.
IAP (SA store, 2026-10-27): 'Text Detective' monthly SAR 59.99; voice investigation week SAR 79.99 / month SAR 199.99; single cases SAR 19.99–34.99; 4-case bundle SAR 84.99.
Cases include hospital deaths, a strangled boy in a park and a body on a yacht; 4.0 from 4 ratings (SA).
athar_applications: Shows Arabic consumers are being offered premium-priced AI interrogation subscriptions now; case themes (child victim) show the content-safety gap ATHAR can own for teens.
limitations: Very few ratings; prices are listing snapshots; case quality not tested.

title: BUSTED: Interrogation — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Released 8 Oct 2026; full Arabic and English; 12+; free-text questioning of five characters, own notes, and confronting two incompatible statements to expose a liar.
New case every six hours; weekly case free; coins and 'Cold Files' IAP SAR 3.49–27.99; ads removable (SAR 14.99); listing states 'Nervousness is not evidence.'
athar_applications: Implements the 'expose contradictions, not pressure' rule ATHAR proposed (KO-PO-09-002) — that design idea is now in market and easy to copy.
limitations: Launched weeks ago; 2 ratings; uses Firebase analytics and ads per listing.

title: Al-Mufattish Fahlawy (المفتش فهلوي) — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Released 27 Aug 2026; 4+; comic Egyptian-neighbourhood crime cases; free-text AI interrogation with suspects replying in Egyptian colloquial; 3 questions per suspect with a stress meter.
UV/magnifier crime-scene search, string evidence board, daily case every 24 hours, police-rank progression, hint power-ups; no ratings yet (SA, 2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Dialect AI suspects and comic tone for younger players are now taken by a solo developer — ATHAR's Arabic-dialect AI is not a moat.
limitations: Description borrows cartoon character names (rights unclear); no ratings; language list on store shows EN only despite Arabic content.

title: Al-Qadiya 001 (القضية ٠٠١) — App Store listing (SA)
authors: DataWeave Company for Communications and IT
key_findings: Released 16 Jul 2026; 12+; 4–10 players at one table examine evidence (photos, messages, recordings, bank statements), question suspects and vote on the killer.
Original cases in Saudi Arabic, a new case weekly; case IAP SAR 3.99–69.00 (2026-10-27); 4.6 from 8 ratings (SA).
athar_applications: Digitizes the paper case-file habit for majlis groups — overlaps KO-PO-09A-006 (hybrid group play).
limitations: Small base; social-vote outcome, not individual reasoning scoring.

title: Tuhma (تهمة) — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Released 2 Sep 2026; Arabic; 9+; 4–12 players in one majlis, one is the killer; four lab reports in Saudi dialect progressively narrow the weapon/object cards; one accusation each.
IAP: Night Pass SAR 9.99; Plus monthly SAR 19.99 (2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Progressive lab reports that move from ambiguous to decisive are a clean, teen-safe evidence-weighting mechanic ATHAR can adapt for classroom group play.
limitations: 2 ratings; social game, no learning claims.

title: Ultra Murdle — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Released 13 Jul 2026; English and Arabic with RTL; 1,355 logic-grid cases in 10 volumes; leaderboard and badges; hint packs SAR 4.99–12.99.
athar_applications: Volume-based Arabic logic mysteries exist; ATHAR should not compete on case count of constraint puzzles.
limitations: 3 ratings; independent developer; uses a Murdle-like name (relationship to Murdle not stated).

title: Detective Files: Mystery Cases — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Released 22 Apr 2026; 19 listing languages including Arabic; 12+; picture-and-clue seating deduction; gem IAP up to SAR 399.99 (2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Hyper-casual publishers now ship Arabic detective-flavoured puzzles — attention competition at the casual end.
limitations: Not an investigation game; 16 ratings in SA.

title: Vodafone Qatar — Shater kids app page
key_findings: Shater: safe, ad-free kids space with 200 games and videos and 100+ educational apps in English and Arabic, with parental control.
Price QR40 per month after a free month (postpaid) or 7 days (prepaid).
athar_applications: A telco-curated Arabic kids catalog with a subscription and parental controls is a ready distribution shelf for ATHAR's younger tier.
limitations: Page undated; App Store listing (Shater Kids) has 3 ratings, so active reach is unclear; content is for young children, not teens.

title: TradeArabia — STC's innovative platforms transform gaming experience
key_findings: Interview at the Esports World Cup with the head of stc play, describing it as a social engagement platform for gamers (match updates, leaderboards, predictions with prizes), alongside five stc tv channels covering the event.
athar_applications: stc's gaming assets centre on esports fandom, not edutainment — a sponsorship/visibility channel rather than a learning-content shelf.
limitations: Publication date not reliably captured (EWC coverage, likely 2024); journalism, not a stc product page (stc official page returned 404).

title: Al-Jarida — Zain partners with Gizer under Zain Esports
title_ar: «زين» تعقد شراكة مع منصة Gizer للألعاب الإلكترونية تحت مظلة Zain Esports
key_findings: 21 Feb 2022: Zain Kuwait partnered with Gizer to offer mobile esports games under the Zain Esports brand, paid via carrier billing (postpaid bill or prepaid balance) without bank cards.
athar_applications: Carrier billing removes the card barrier for teen purchases — a payment rail ATHAR could use with operator partners.
limitations: Esports, not education; 2022 status may have changed.

title: Israel Ministry of Education — 'Escape Room' teacher kit, grades 1–3 (Arabic edition, PDF)
title_ar: طقم المعلم: غرفة الهروب للصفوف أ–ج
key_findings: 23-page Arabic teacher kit (PDF metadata created Jan 2025) for an AI-literacy classroom escape game for grades 1–3: frame story, station puzzles, teacher answers and hints, printable certificates.
athar_applications: Evidence that ministry-made Arabic classroom escape kits exist, but for young children and AI literacy, not investigation reasoning for teens.
limitations: Outside ATHAR's Arab target markets; young age band; publisher identified from domain and Hebrew file title.

title: Qatar Museums — Dadu Investigator Camp
authors: Qatar Museums / Dadu, Children's Museum of Qatar
key_findings: 27–31 Jul 2025, ages 8–11: children examine mock crime scenes, analyse evidence, record and organise information and present findings in teams; tickets required.
athar_applications: Gulf cultural institutions already run forensic-themed reasoning camps — a partner channel for ATHAR's summer and museum programmes.
limitations: Past one-week event; younger than ATHAR's core band; price not shown.

title: Gulf Today — Children project their inner detectives (SCRF 2019)
key_findings: At the Sharjah Children's Reading Festival 2019, ex-police detectives and forensic experts ran a crime-scene workshop where children matched shoeprints and studied fingerprint patterns in competing teams.
athar_applications: Demand signal for hands-on forensic learning at Gulf children's events; ATHAR's digital micro-labs could extend such workshops.
limitations: 2019; one event; organiser names not given.

title: Savvy Games Group publishes Annual Report for 2024
key_findings: 25 Aug 2025: Savvy (strategy launched Sep 2022, chaired by the Crown Prince) reports pillars of game development/publishing, esports and KSA ecosystem; names Scopely (MONOPOLY GO! passed $3B revenue), ESL FACEIT Group and Riyadh-based Steer Studios' first mobile soft launch.
Describes Savvy as the National Champion for the National Gaming and Esports Strategy (NGES).
athar_applications: The Saudi state-backed games champion invests in mass-market mobile and esports, not educational mystery — low direct threat, but a possible funder/publisher if ATHAR proves traction.
limitations: Company self-report; portfolio details beyond those named not checked.

title: Manga Productions launches Nioh 3 in Arabic
key_findings: 8 Feb 2026: Manga Productions (subsidiary of the Misk Foundation) launched Nioh 3 in Arabic on PS5 and Steam as Koei Tecmo's MENA publisher, with Saudi talent in publishing, marketing and localization.
athar_applications: A Saudi publisher with a localization pipeline for Japanese games could localize or co-publish a premium detective title — medium-term competitive risk and partnership option.
limitations: Company news; no detective/mystery title announced.

title: PocketGamer.biz — Ash Games Studio secures $1.5m seed funding
key_findings: 24 Jul 2026: Saudi Ash Games Studio (founded 2022) raised $1.5M led by Merak Capital's gaming fund with Impact46; builds story-driven PC/console games from Saudi stories; known for Azooma Escape (Aug 2025); next title Nomad: The Legend of Zarqa.
athar_applications: Shows Saudi VC money flowing to culturally rooted narrative games — a sign investors will fund Arab-story IP, and that a funded studio could enter mystery.
limitations: Trade press; funding amount as reported.

title: Azooma Escape — Steam store page
key_findings: Released 20 Aug 2025; $14.99; 14 languages including Arabic; reverse-stealth comedy of escaping a family gathering; Steam: 89% of 77 reviews (2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Gulf family-life humour travels in Arabic and English — cultural setting can be an asset, but scale so far is small.
limitations: Small review base; not a mystery game.

title: HUMAIN Chat — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Released 24 Aug 2025; Arabic and English; free; 4.5 from 1,968 ratings (SA, 2026-10-27); developer page lists HUMAIN; support URL chat.humain.ai.
Listing says the app runs on ALLaM 34B, built and hosted in Saudi Arabia, with Arabic voice input and optional web search.
athar_applications: Confirms a free, consumer-grade Arabic LLM chat in Saudi teens' hands — anyone can improvise a 'detective chat', so ATHAR's value must come from authored, fair, assessed cases. ALLaM hosting in-Kingdom may matter for Saudi school data rules.
limitations: Self-description; model quality for in-character play untested.

title: ALLaM-7B-Instruct-preview — Hugging Face model card
key_findings: 7B Arabic–English model trained from scratch (4T English + 1.2T mixed tokens) by SDAIA's National Center for AI; 4,096-token context; card metadata licence Apache-2.0 (body refers to a LICENSE file).
Card warns developers to add their own safety measures.
athar_applications: Candidate on-device/small model for constrained Arabic suspect replies (as Homicide Desk does locally); short context limits long case files.
limitations: Preview release; licence wording should be checked in the LICENSE file before commercial use.

title: Jais-3-32B — Hugging Face model card (Inception42 / MBZUAI IFM / Cerebras)
key_findings: Jais 3 family published 29 Sep 2026 (0.9B to 375B-A23B variants); the 32B model is Arabic–English with a 512K context window, Apache-2.0, intended for assistant and agentic uses including reasoning and tool use.
Card benchmarks include dialectal Arabic tests and compare against other open models (not re-checked here).
athar_applications: Open Arabic models with long context make 'whole case file in context' AI suspects cheap — lowers the cost for every competitor, including ATHAR.
limitations: Benchmarks are self-reported on the card; safety behaviour for minors not documented.

title: Fanar-2-27B-Instruct — Hugging Face model card (QCRI, HBKU)
license: Apache-2.0 (per card metadata; Gemma base terms may apply)
key_findings: Released Mar 2026; continued pretraining of Gemma-3-27B on ~166B Arabic/English tokens; supports MSA and Gulf, Levantine and Egyptian dialects; 32,768-token context; sponsored by Qatar's MCIT; consumer chat and mobile apps exist.
Card states alignment with Islamic values and Arabic culture.
athar_applications: A dialect-aware regional model with explicit cultural alignment is a natural candidate for teen-safe Arabic characters; Gemma base licence terms also apply.
limitations: Card metadata says Apache-2.0 but base-model terms may add conditions; check before commercial use.

title: Tamatem — Girls' Secrets: Choose Your Fate (اسرار البنات) — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Arabic interactive-story app with 20+ stories (romance, drama, comedy, fantasy); 9+; 4.4 from 9,991 ratings (SA, 2026-10-27); gem and ticket IAP SAR 9.99–89.99.
athar_applications: Proves a regional publisher can run a choice-narrative app at scale in Arabic — the closest proven format to ATHAR's story layer, without investigation or assessment.
limitations: Romance/drama focus; no mystery line found in this listing.

title: Ajel — Critical Thinking among subjects added to the curriculum (2021)
title_ar: مادة التفكير الناقد.. أبرز المواد التي تمت إضافتها للمناهج الدراسية
key_findings: 31 Aug 2021: the Saudi MoE announced 34 new curricula including a Critical Thinking subject for intermediate and secondary stages, aimed at reducing rote learning and ideological influence.
athar_applications: Updates the course status beyond 2018–2019: by 2021 critical thinking had moved into intermediate as well as secondary curricula — a broader school hook for class-length cases.
limitations: Newspaper report; 2026 timetable placement still unverified (a 2025 homework-help site references a first-secondary 'Critical Thinking' textbook, not cataloged).

title: Escape Hunt Dubai — games page
key_findings: Dubai rooms listed (2026-10-27): Curse of the Pharaoh, Journey to Atlantis, Alice in Puzzleland, Aladdin & the Magic Vault, Prison Breakout; plus print-and-play (incl. 'Murder at the Mansion') and a digital game; corporate team building.
athar_applications: Escape Hunt now sells print-and-play murder mysteries alongside rooms — a low-cost format overlapping ATHAR's group cases; no school or Arabic offer visible.
limitations: Page language of games and prices not captured.

title: Abwaab — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Grades 4–12 curriculum video lessons, question bank, timed assessments and a WhatsApp 'Morshed' study coach; 4.2 from 3,339 ratings (SA, 2026-10-27).
IAP: Saudi grade packages SAR 95–130.99, Qudurat plan SAR 149.99, Tahsili SAR 129.99, live sessions SAR 279.99 (2026-10-27).
athar_applications: Confirms Abwaab sells exam-prep packages, not reasoning or investigation content — a channel, not a competitor, for ATHAR.
limitations: Listing language metadata shows EN only though content is Arabic; prices are store snapshots.
